subject: PulseQuark - US-EAST1 throughput collapse and staged cross-region intake
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@pulsequark.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@pulsequark.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput collapse in US-EAST1 — urgent help needed

David / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sharp drop in successful requests from our EU and US customers routing through your US-EAST1 AZ around 13:45 PT — 60-70% error rate for generation calls and a 3x latency increase for the requests that succeed. This started impacting checkout flows and live chat. Attached is a short CSV with the minute-level TPS and error breakdown (pq_kpi_timeseries.csv).

Current asks:
- Immediate mitigation path (cross-region intake or routing) to reduce user impact.
- Short ETA for a rollback or a temporary model fallback if this is model-side.
- Telemetry we should provide to speed root cause triage.

Priya and I are on standby; we can jump on a bridge. This is P0 for PulseQuark.

—Alex
Head of Platform Engineering
PulseQuark

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@pulsequark.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@pulsequark.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 14:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse in US-EAST1 — urgent help needed

Alex / Priya — thanks for the heads up and the CSV. We're activating a rapid response. Short summary of immediate actions we are initiating now:

1) Traffic drainer: we'll start an automated spill from the affected US-EAST1 AZ to US-WEST2 for new sessions within the next 5-10 minutes. That should reduce load quickly while keeping stateful clients intact.
2) Model fallback: if latency stays elevated after spill, we'll force-route to a quantized variant (latency-optimized) for non-critical generation paths.
3) Telemetry: please share any client-side request IDs and the example request payloads that are seeing 5xx errors — that helps map the KV cache interaction.

I'm looping in Neha for the playbook and Ben for the commercial/exec comms. We'll keep you posted every 15 minutes.

On the bridge if helpful: +1-650-555-0122

—David
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

> 1) Traffic drainer: we'll start an automated spill from the affected US-EAST1 AZ to US-WEST2 for new sessions within the next 5-10 minutes.

Alex / team,

Quick operational note and the plan I executed:
- I kicked the staged-drain play (redwood-staged-failover-playbook.pdf) for PulseQuark. This will keep existing KV-cached sessions pinned to US-EAST1 for 30s to avoid token duplication, then prefer US-WEST2 for new session creation. Expected reduction in request failure surface: ~65% within 12 minutes.
- We've enabled additional autoscaling for the dedicated pool in US-WEST2 and pre-warmed the quantized model shard so fallback is near-instant if we need it.
- Collected a sample set of 20 failed request IDs (first batch) and pushed them to your S3 share for correlation. Link sent to your Priya.

Next steps for debugging (if the spill does not remediate):
- Check inter-AZ control-plane error logs for timeout amplifications (I suspect a k-v cache eviction storm).
- If we confirm the KV eviction, we'll apply an emergency K/V cache throttle and move long-running sessions to the stateful eviction-safe lane.

I'll post an updated telemetry dump and the bridge URL in 10m.

—Neha
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 18:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse in US-EAST1 — urgent help needed

Alex / Priya — post-incident summary and next steps.

Status as of 18:30 PT:
- Automated spill to US-WEST2 completed; customer-visible error rate reduced from ~65% to ~6% over a 25-minute window. Latency for new sessions stabilized to near-baseline on the quantized variant.
- Root cause (preliminary): accelerated K/V cache evictions in US-EAST1 triggered by an unusually dense prefix distribution from PulseQuark's high-concurrency checkout traffic combined with a concurrent autoscaling lag on our serving fleet. We have a follow-up RCA scheduled for tomorrow with PulseQuark engineers.

Immediate remediation steps agreed:
- We'll provision an increased K/V cache headroom for PulseQuark in US-EAST1 for two weeks while they implement a shorter prefix TTL on long-lived sessions.
- Redwood will provide a targeted config for client-side retry/backoff to reduce parallelism spikes and avoid rehydration storms.
- Comms: Ben will send the customer-facing note. David will share the telemetry dump and the list of failed request IDs we collected.

Attachments: updated playbook (redwood-staged-failover-playbook.pdf) and minute-level KPI dump (pq_kpi_timeseries.csv).

Thank you for working through this quickly — we'll keep the RCA narrow and action-oriented.

—Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
